speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long the skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lesions being painless and nonpruritic, along with the daycare exposure, are quite telling. Have you noticed any fluid-filled blisters or crusting on the lesions, and are they located anywhere else besides the abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of pearly papules with central umbilication is highly characteristic of Molluscum contagiosum. To confirm, I will examine the lesions more closely and check for any signs of secondary infection or involvement of the face or eyelids.

REQUEST TEST: Dermoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal dermoscopy results are consistent with the clinical presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules. Do the lesions express a white, cheesy core when gently squeezed, and have you noticed any spreading to the face or genital area?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical presentation of painless, pearly, umbilicated papules in a daycare-attending child is classic for Molluscum contagiosum.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
